title: Arakawa Under the Bridge
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kou Ichinomiya, a rich young man raised never to owe anyone, is saved from the river by Nino, a homeless woman who says she is from Venus. To repay her he agrees to teach her about love, and he moves under the bridge as 'Recruit', joining an eccentric riverbank community that includes a mayor in a kappa costume, a star-helmeted musician and a gun-toting man in a nun's habit. Surreal comedy by Hikaru Nakamura; published in English by Vertical.
life_message: A good life is found in mutual dependence and accepting others as they are, not in money, status or owing nothing.

content.note: Slapstick; Sister, a war veteran in a nun's habit, fires a machine gun and lays booby traps (Wikipedia; ANN).
Slow romance between Kou and Nino; a former yakuza wife and her lover in a comic affair; Kou's secretary implied to be infatuated with him (Wikipedia).
Hoshi buys cigarettes (Wikipedia); not a focus.
Kou has asthma attacks when indebted; a resident walks only on white lines out of fear (Wikipedia), played as comedy.
Living under a bridge shown as a happy choice.

dominant: Community over money; absurd comedy; acceptance of eccentrics

frames.aligns: Kou learns gift and gratitude among the poor riverbank community.
frames.concerns: Sister, a man in a nun's habit, holds a seconds-long 'mass' firing a machine gun.

frames.aligns: Humility: a proud heir humbled under the bridge.
frames.concerns: Parody church under an Orthodox cross; comic adultery subplot.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kou's pride in owing nothing is gently dismantled (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Riverbank residents live outside Tokyo's rules.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Found family replaces Kou's wealthy father (AniList Found Family).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rich heir becomes the 'Recruit' under a kappa 'Mayor'.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folk figures (kappa) mixed with modern city life.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Eccentric self-expression celebrated over career success.

folkways.japan: Plays on Japanese ideas of obligation and repaying debts (on and giri) and on the senpai-kohai style 'Recruit' title within a group.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers call it heartfelt; one finds the social critique muddled by tone; none call it preachy.

personified.ideology: never owe anyone; status and self-sufficiency
corporate rule of never being indebted

delivery.note: Kou's father is cold and plans to destroy the riverbank, yet is shown to love his son (Wikipedia), so the creed is teased, not demonized.

winners_losers: Kou wins a home and love by giving up his creed of never owing; the riverbank misfits win sympathy over the status-driven world.
to_verify: Only volume 1 reviewed; later volumes summarized from Wikipedia character list only.
Sister's machine-gun 'mass' under an Orthodox cross may concern some Christian readers; check its tone.
